questions.title: GATE EE 2018 | GA Question: 7
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
The following C function takes a single-linked list of integers as a parameter and rearranges the elements of the list. The function is called with the list containing the integers $1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7$ in the given order. What will be the contents of the list after function completes execution?

struct node {
    int value;
    struct node *next;
};

void rearrange(struct node *list) {
    struct node *p, *q;
    int temp;
    if (!list || !list -> next) return;
    p = list; q = list -> next;
    while(q) {
        temp = p -> value; p->value =  q -> value;
        q->value = temp; p = q ->next;
        q = p? p ->next : 0;
    }   
}

questions.subject: Power Systems & Protection
questions.question: A $400\text{ kV}$, 3-phase lossless transmission line has total series inductance $L = 1.0\text{ mH/km}$ and shunt capacitance $C = 0.01\,\mu\text{F/km}$. The surge impedance $Z_c = \sqrt{L/C}$ (in Ohms) of the line is ________.
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Power Systems & Protection):

$Z_c = \sqrt{\frac{L}{C}} = \sqrt{\frac{1.0 \times 10^{-3}}{0.01 \times 10^{-6}}} = \sqrt{10^5} = 316.23\,\Omega$.

questions.question: The open-loop transfer function of a unity feedback system is $G(s) = \frac{K}{s(s+2)(s+4)}$. Using Routh-Hurwitz stability criterion, the maximum value of $K$ for closed-loop stability is ________.
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Control Systems):

Characteristic equation: $1 + G(s) = 0 \implies s(s^2 + 6s + 8) + K = 0 \implies s^3 + 6s^2 + 8s + K = 0$. Routh array first column entries: $s^3: 1$, $s^2: 6$, $s^1: \frac{6(8) - K}{6} = \frac{48 - K}{6}$, $s^0: K$. For stability, all terms must be positive: $48 - K > 0 \implies K < 48$.

questions.question: A single-phase full-wave controlled bridge rectifier is fed from a $230\text{ V}$ (RMS), $50\text{ Hz}$ AC source. The firing angle is $\alpha = 60^\circ$. Assuming continuous conduction, the average DC output voltage $V_{dc} = \frac{2 V_m}{\pi} \cos \alpha$ (in Volts) is ________ (round off to one decimal place).
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Power Electronics & Drives):
